title: Nikon 25.79 mm eyepiece optical system, 26.22 deg half field (numerical example 1)

collection.attribution: Nikon Corporation, US10527839B2. The prescription is the published numerical example; the native Project is a transcription of its table, reversed so the eyepiece forms a real image plane.
collection.redistribution: The numerical prescription is published in a granted patent, a public record. The transcription, the native Project and this evidence extract are distributed under MIT. The patent document itself is not redistributed.

aperture_validity.basis: The aperture-stop plate extends beyond its opening.
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: No pupil, illumination or MTF evidence is recorded, so no stop-dependent match is claimed.
aperture_validity.consequence: The record supports first-order and structural queries; a stop-dependent constraint stays unconfirmed.

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: The publication prints one reference wavelength in air; it is converted once to the vacuum wavelength the engine evaluates.
spectrum.wavelength_precision: A single sample; no rounding in the Project.

sampling_span_nm.note: a zero-width interval cannot be filtered: the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around the one stated sample. The sample itself is sampling_wavelengths_nm; the window is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: The example states one reference wavelength only.

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: Thick-lens ABCD through the committed Project at the reference wavelength.

comparison.rule: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * |source|. atol covers the printed precision of the stated focal length; rtol covers the printed precision of the radii and thicknesses, the constant-index material model and the engine's air-referenced index convention.

back_focal_length.basis: The source prints no back focal length, so this quantity has no source value.

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Effective focal length as printed for the example
nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.conditions: Reference wavelength (587.562 nm in air); object at infinity.

entrance_pupil_diameter_mm.definition: Diameter of the nominal 4 mm eye pupil plane placed 18 mm in front of the first surface. The publication states no pupil size, so this is the modelling choice the aperture basis describes, not a source value.

entrance_pupil_f_number.definition: Magnitude of effective focal length divided by the admitted axial entrance pupil diameter.

field.definition: Field angle; the full field is twice the stated half field
field.note: The printed half angle of view is stated at a -1 m^-1 dioptre setting.

materials.basis: Every element is a constant index equal to its printed nd, valid at the reference wavelength only; the printed vd values are kept in the evidence extract.

approximations.statement: Each element is a constant index equal to its printed nd, valid only at the reference wavelength; the printed vd values are kept in the evidence extract but are not modelled.

The publication states no clear semi-diameters. Each element is given one clear diameter: the largest of the paraxial marginal-ray and chief-ray envelopes over its own surfaces (marginal ray through a nominal 4 mm eye pupil, chief ray at the printed half field), times a 2 per cent mechanical margin. The envelope is a minimum clear aperture, so every surface of the element passes the axial beam and the chief ray at the full printed field. It is a buildable estimate, not a drawing: no vignetting beyond the stop is modelled and no vignetting figure is claimed.

notes: The engine's paraxial focal length is compared with the printed fa = 25.79 mm.
The printed conditional expressions are kept in the evidence extract, not re-evaluated.

The printed table ends with a plane in air, which the reversal keeps as the last surface before the image plane; it has no optical power and the importer carries it as a dummy surface (reported as DUMMY_SURFACE).
